title: Forces, Friction and Newton's First Law

items.title: Today's lesson
items.content:
A shopping-trolley puzzle opens the lesson: let go and it stops, so **does a moving thing need a push to keep moving?**

One carton of books that Riya pushes across the floor then carries the idea: net force, friction, and a floor with no friction that leads to **Newton's first law**.

A bus that brakes suddenly brings in **inertia**.

items.title: You already know
items.content:
• a force is a push or a pull

• velocity has a direction

• acceleration means the velocity changes in size, direction or both

• position–time and velocity–time graphs for rest and for uniform motion

items.title: By the end, you can
items.content:
**1.** Tell balanced from unbalanced forces and find the net force along a line.

**2.** Explain friction and its effect on motion.

**3.** State Newton's first law and explain inertia with examples.

**Answer to Question 7**

$30 + 20 = 50\ \text{N}$, **to the right**.

items.prompt: A weightlifter holds a barbell steady above his head. The forces on the barbell are
options: its weight downwards and his push upwards; balanced
its weight downwards and his push upwards; unbalanced

items.prompt: Three forces act on a block, as shown. The net force on the block is

items.text:
**On Question 1**

The Earth's pull (its weight) acts downwards and the lifter's push upwards. The barbell stays at rest, so they are **balanced**.

**On Question 2**

$8 + 5 = 13\ \text{N}$ to the right; $15 - 13 = 2\ \text{N}$, along the larger force, **to the left**.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• Riya pushes the carton on her own with **20 N**.

• The carton **does not move**.

**Answer to Question 10**

**Zero.** It stays at rest, so the forces are balanced.

**Answer to Question 11**

**Friction** from the floor: $20\ \text{N}$, **to the left**, opposite to her push.

**Answer to Question 12**

**Her push.** Now there is a net force in the direction of motion.

**Answer to Question 13**

It **slows down and stops**. Only friction acts now, opposite to the motion.

Questions 10 to 13 in order. Answers are on pointers 2 to 5.
Draw the friction arrow on the board only after Question 11.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• A stack of coins shot along three surfaces by the **same** stretch of a rubber band.

• How far the coins slide on each.

**Answer to Question 14**

The **marble floor**. There the coins slow down most slowly and travel the farthest.

**Answer to Question 15**

The **nature of the two surfaces** in contact. Rougher surfaces give more friction.

items.prompt: True or false? (i) Friction acts in the same direction as the motion. (ii) A carton that does not move when pushed has no friction acting on it. (iii) A ball given the same push rolls farther on a smooth floor than on grass. The true statements are
A girl pushes a heavy box with 15 N, and it does not move. She pushes with 25 N, and it still does not move. The force of friction on the box is

items.text:
**On Question 1**

(i) False: friction acts **opposite** to the motion.

(ii) False: friction **balances** the push.

(iii) True: the smooth floor has less friction.

**On Question 2**

While the box stays at rest, friction **matches** the push, opposite to it each time.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• The same coin lanes, now with the fourth lane uncovered: a surface with **no friction**.

**Answer to Question 16**

The coins slow down **more slowly** and go **farther** each time.

**Answer to Question 17**

**No.** Nothing acts against their motion, so they keep moving at the same velocity forever.

**Answer to Question 18**

**No.** It stopped because **friction** acted on it. The puck glides far because the air-hockey table has very little friction.

items.text:
**Answer to Question 19**

• At rest: the position–time graph is a **horizontal line**; the velocity–time graph lies **on the time axis**.

• Constant velocity: the position–time graph is a **straight sloping line**; the velocity–time graph is a **horizontal line**.

script.x: Question 19. Let students sketch both cases first. Answer is on pointer 1.
Then reveal the graphs.

items.prompt: On which of these is the net force zero?
options: a car going round a circular track at a steady 30 km/h
a train moving along a straight track at a steady 60 km/h
an apple falling from a tree
a cyclist braking to a stop

items.prompt: Assertion (A): A moving object needs a net force to keep it moving.  Reason (R): If no net force acts on a moving object, it continues to move with a constant velocity.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

items.prompt: Riya now keeps the carton sliding at a steady speed in a straight line by pushing it with 40 N. The force of friction on it is
options: 40 N, in the direction of her push
zero, because the carton is moving
more than 40 N, opposite to her push

items.text:
**On Question 1**

The train's speed and direction are both constant. The car changes direction, the apple speeds up and the cyclist slows down.

**On Question 2**

A net force is needed only to **change** the velocity, not to keep it.

**On Question 3**

The velocity is constant, so the net force is **zero**: friction equals her push, $40\ \text{N}$, opposite to it.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• Left: the bus **starts** suddenly.

• Right: the bus **brakes** suddenly.

• Watch the standing passengers.

**Answer to Question 20**

Their feet move forward with the bus, but the upper body **tends to stay at rest**.

**Answer to Question 21**

Their feet stop with the bus, but the upper body **tends to keep moving** forward.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• A coin rests on a card over a glass.

• The card is flicked away quickly, and the coin drops into the glass.

**Answer to Question 22**

The quick flick acts on the **card**. The coin tends to stay at rest, so it is left behind and falls into the glass.

**Answer to Question 23**

The **loaded** one. It has more mass, so it has more inertia.

items.prompt: Dust comes out of a hanging carpet when it is beaten with a stick, because
options: the stick moves the carpet suddenly, but the dust tends to stay at rest
the stick pushes the dust particles out of the carpet
the dust becomes heavier when the carpet is hit
the moving stick blows air through the carpet

items.prompt: Which of these has the most inertia?

items.text:
**On Question 1**

The stick suddenly moves the carpet, but the dust particles tend to stay at rest because of their **inertia**. So they separate from the carpet and fall.

**On Question 2**

The loaded truck has the largest **mass**, so it has the most inertia.
